Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1220 PM EST Sat Nov 14 2026
 

- A narrow corridor of lake effect rain showers (briefly mixed with
  melting snow) persists today and tonight, mainly along the southern
  Lake Huron shoreline. 

- Mostly cloudy skies expected elsewhere through the weekend. 

- Brisk morning winds drop wind chills into the 20s (isolated upper
  teens) Sunday morning.

- Dry weather expected area-wide Monday through Thursday with a
  steady warming trend. 

&&

.AVIATION...

Surface high pressure spans a broad area from northern Ontario to 
the Gulf coast, along the MS river valley, but is slow to move 
eastward this afternoon and tonight. This maintains NW flow that is 
cold enough to support widespread activation of Great Lakes clouds 
across Lower Mi through at least Sunday morning. Satellite and 
surface observations leading into this afternoon report MVFR below 
2000 ft across the region that grinds up above 2000 ft with a few 
breaks at times during peak daytime heating. Model soundings 
indicate an adequate subsidence inversion developing just in time to 
trap broken MVFR tonight and Sunday morning. Another round of 
diurnal enhancement fights against inbound high pressure for slow 
improvement Sunday afternoon. 

For DTW... Ceiling remains below 5000 ft during any breaks of MVFR 
this afternoon. NW wind off the slightly higher terrain is also 
capable of producing MVFR ceiling variability tonight through 
Sunday. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

*  High for ceiling at or below 5,000 feet this afternoon and 
   tonight.
